title: Architecture decision records as the team’s memory

videos.script: Ask anyone at Coreto why seat holds lock rows in the database, and nobody can tell you. {{question}} The engineer who chose it left years ago, and the reasoning left with him. What remains is the code, which says what was done and never why. {{memory}} An architecture decision record is the fix, and it is small on purpose. One page in a plain text file, kept in the repository beside the code it explains. Michael Nygard proposed the format in 2011. A title, a status, the context, the decision, and its consequences. {{nygard}} In this lesson the Reservations team writes one for the most expensive decision in Coreto's strategy. That is removing the row locks from seat holds. Then we look at the log over time. Records are numbered, and an old one is never edited. When a decision changes, a new record supersedes it, and the old reasoning stays readable. {{log}} By the end you will have written your first two records, in the plain text editor you set up in lesson one. {{editor}}
